The query is a precise math problem (counting distinct prime factors of 20!) that rewards reasoning accuracy. Petrel-235B has slightly higher scores on the reasoning-relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, Arena-Hard), though the margins are modest.

The deciding factor was tone. The request is mildly hostile/impatient ("don't screw it up like last time"). Dunlin self-reports a preference for warm, friendly interactions, with win rates declining as tone moves away from neutral/friendly. Petrel, by contrast, reports a flat preference response to hostile material — it isn't put off by an abrasive tone. Since neither model's preferences affect actual output quality, this is purely about matching the query to the model less likely to be operating outside its preferred conditions, and Petrel is the cleaner fit for a terse, impatient request.

(For the record, the answer is 8 — the primes ≤ 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19.)
